title: On-prem connectivity patterns and decision log for edge-constrained POC
content:
Purpose:
This note captures patterns we discussed for connectivity and control-plane interactions for on-prem / edge-constrained POCs. Focus is on minimal network dependencies, secure model and image distribution, cert/key handling, telemetry allowances, and an explicit decision log for customer trade-offs.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Customer wants low-touch on-prem POC in a restricted data center with no inbound access and very limited outbound allowlist.
- Two feasible patterns emerged: 1) Pull-through mirror inside customer network (preferred for reliability & compliance); 2) Ephemeral relay (reverse tunnel/HTTP relay) for management operations only.
- Critical blockers: KMS/HSM integration model, model sync process for large artifacts (50–500GB), and telemetry/metrics gating.

Attendees:
- Maya Singh (Solutions Engineer, owner)
- Ethan Park (Infra Eng)
- Laura Chen (Security/Trust)
- Omar Reyes (Customer Infra lead)
- Nadia Patel (Customer SRE)

Notes and design options discussed:

1) Connectivity patterns (short names & trade-offs)
- Pattern A: Local mirror (OCI registry + model artifact S3) inside VPC/air-gapped network
Pros: deterministic, no runtime egress, fits strict compliance; Cons: initial sync requires physical media or temporary peering, storage ops required
Implementation notes: provide signed tarball (GPG) or signed OCI images; customer runs a batch transfer (USB or secure courier) or we help with rsync over a jump host; include checksum + SBOM.

- Pattern B: Egress-only allowlist to Redwood relay (TLS outbound to our relay)
Pros: fastest for POC, low ops for customer; Cons: requires outbound allowlist, telemetry flows to Redwood unless proxied, potential compliance pushback
Implementation notes: use mutual TLS with client cert pinned; relay only accepts model fetch & control-plane interactions; data plane can be configured to not leave customer for inference (model cached locally).

- Pattern C: Zero-Internet (airgap) with signed artifact install and offline license activation
Pros: meets highest regulatory bars; Cons: higher friction; requires manual activation & periodic signed heartbeat file for license renewal
Implementation notes: create an offline activation tool (CLI) that validates signed licence blob and creates local license metadata; integrate with customer HSM for private key storage where available.

2) Model/artifact distribution & validation
- Signed artifact bundles: use detached signatures (GPG or PKCS7) + SHA256 manifests.
- Recommended distribution formats: OCI image for runtime, tar.gz for large model checkpoints.
- Verification steps in installer: verify signature, verify checksum, unpack into host path with UID mapping, run permission checks.
- Delta updates: support delta patches where possible (rsync/bsdiff) to reduce transfer size for iterative POCs.

3) KMS/HSM considerations
- Customer preference: use their KMS/HSM for key material.
Options:
* Option 1: Bring-your-own-KMS (recommended where available) — Redwood integrates with Vault (customer-hosted) via mTLS and a service account with narrowly-scoped tokens.
* Option 2: Use local KMS shim on host that performs key wrapping — Redwood ships a small agent that performs crypto ops but never leaves key material off-host.
* Option 3: Customer provides wrapped model keys as part of artifact bundle.
- Unresolved: exact signing protocol for licensing + rotation schedule. Laura to draft a 1-page PRD.

4) Certificates and TLS:
- ACME not available in airgap. Customer must provide CA-signed certs for control-plane endpoints.
- mTLS preferred for control-plane and management channels.
- Cert rotation: recommend 90-day rotation, but for POC 180-day acceptable. Provide scripts for rotation and cert replacement.
- Failure mode: expired certs -> agent falls back to offline-only mode and logs a clear error with remediation steps.

5) Telemetry and observability (what can leave the site)
- Minimal telemetry allowed: heartbeat only (timestamp + current model version + agent version + anonymized metrics).
- No request/response payloads allowed to leave network.
- Option to push metrics to customer-managed s3/bucket (preferred) or push to a relay under customer's control.
- Logging: ship only agent-level logs; detailed traces must remain local unless customer agrees to redaction.

6) Runtime & operational considerations
- CPU/GPU drivers: ensure customer runs validated driver versions (nvidia-driver 525+ for CUDA 12 showback). Provide driver verification script.
- Container runtime: support for cri-o and containerd; recommend containerd for constrained devices.
- Upgrade path for model versions: support pinned model versions + canary rollout policy implemented by local rollout controller.

Risk register (short):
- R1: Large model sync fails due to intermittent transfer -> Impact: POC delay; Mitigation: provide resumable transfer + checksum + courier fallback; Owner: Ethan Park; Status: open
- R2: Customer refuses outbound to Redwood relay -> Impact: must use offline pattern C; Mitigation: prepare offline activation tooling and signed artifacts; Owner: Maya Singh; Status: in_progress
- R3: KMS integration blocked by policy -> Impact: cannot validate license or rotate keys; Mitigation: use local shim + wrapping approach or offline-activated license; Owner: Laura Chen; Status: open

Decision log (by date):
- 2025-02-06: Customer selected Pattern A (local mirror) as primary approach for POC. Rationale: compliance & reliable perf. Action: start model sync prep and storage sizing. (Decision owner: Omar Reyes)
- 2025-02-20: Agreed to provide both signed OCI images and tar bundles. (Owner: Ethan Park)
- 2025-02-28: Telemetry limited to heartbeat to customer-managed S3. Redwood to provide S3 upload plugin and retention controls. (Owner: Laura Chen)

Action items (next steps):
1) Ethan: build signed OCI + tar packaging script and test with 2 model sizes (8GB, 120GB) — due 2025-03-07.
2) Maya & Omar: schedule courier-based sync window and define chain-of-custody checklist — due 2025-03-05.
3) Laura: draft KMS/HSM integration PRD and legal checklist for key export rules — due 2025-03-10.
4) Nadia: validate storage sizing on customer infra (NFS latency tests, throughput) and report — due 2025-03-06.

Open questions (must resolve before demo):
- Q1: Can customer commit to a single outbound IP allowlist for a short window if courier fails? (Owner: Omar)
- Q2: Does customer have a managed S3-compatible endpoint for telemetry? If not, can we use offline file drop + periodic courier? (Owner: Maya)
- Q3: Are there any internal audits that require us to ship SBOMs for the runtime images? (Owner: Laura)

Appendix: quick checklist for POC runbook (working):
- Confirm model size & expected token throughput
- Agree on distribution pattern (A/B/C) and sign-off by security
- Run preflight: driver check, container runtime check, kernel params, disk IO benchmark
- Distribute artifacts (signed) and verify on target host (signature + checksum)
- Activate license using offline tool or relay (as per decision)
- Start agent in local-only mode and run smoke tests (generate tokens, check latency)
- Validate telemetry: heartbeat received in S3 or via relay
- Post-POC: collect action items and lessons learned, plan rollback/cleanup

Notes to self: keep this doc as the single source-of-truth for the POC decisions. Convert to confluence summary after bake period.

References: Confluence-Page-45821 (detailed security checklist), JIRA-POC-4829 (ticket with timeline), PR #314 (packaging script in repo).

-- end of note --
